subject.title: Cron tool schema missing model/timeout/contextTokens/maxSpendUsd fields

question: Should cron jobs gain first-class enforced `contextTokens` and `maxSpendUsd` payload fields, or should those limits be handled through existing agent/model config and broader budget enforcement work?
rationale: The remaining fields are not only missing schema entries; they create new public cron payload/CLI semantics and a spend-enforcement policy that current code does not define.

options.title: Define enforced cron fields
options.body: Add `contextTokens` and `maxSpendUsd` as cron-owned payload fields with protocol, persistence, runtime enforcement, CLI/docs, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Split spend into budget work
options.body: Land only a defined cron context cap here and keep spend caps under the broader gateway budget tracker.

options.title: Document existing controls
options.body: Decline new cron payload fields for now and document current `model`, `timeoutSeconds`, `lightContext`, and `toolsAllow` controls instead.

recommendation.title: Define enforced cron fields
recommendation.body: Add `contextTokens` and `maxSpendUsd` as cron-owned payload fields with protocol, persistence, runtime enforcement, CLI/docs, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest repeated history across the cron normalization/runtime surface and configuration policy guardrails.
